references.text: All the people came early in the morning to him at the temple to hear him – [ref:Luk 21:38|Luke 21:38] confirms that the crowd was eager to listen to Jesus in the temple, which corresponds to all the people hanging on his words and listening.

The chief priests and the scribes sought to lay hands on him, but they feared the people – [ref:Luk 20:19|Luke 20:19] shows that the religious leaders wanted to arrest Jesus but were hindered by the people's support for him.

The chief priests and the scribes sought a way to have Jesus killed, for they feared the people – [ref:Luk 22:2|Luke 22:2] continues the theme of the leaders' murder plots and their fear of the people's reaction.

The chief priests and the scribes heard this and sought a way to get rid of him, for they feared him because all the crowd was amazed at his teaching – [ref:Mark 11:18|Mark 11:18] is a parallel to this verse in Mark, with the same motif of the leaders' fear and the people's enthusiasm.
They sought to seize him, but they feared the crowd – [ref:Mark 12:12|Mark 12:12] shows again that the presence of the people protected Jesus from the leaders' plans.

The chief priests and the Pharisees understood that he was speaking about them and sought to seize him, but they feared the crowds because they held him for a prophet – [ref:Matt 21:45-46|Matthew 21:45-46] is Matthew's parallel where the leaders' desire to arrest Jesus is prevented by the people's favor.

Some wanted to seize him, but no one laid hands on him. The servants came back and said, "Never has anyone spoken like this" – [ref:Joh 7:44-46|John 7:44-46] shows a similar situation where attempts to arrest Jesus failed, partly due to the powerful impact of his words.
All gave witness to him and marveled at the gracious words that came from his mouth – [ref:Luk 4:22|Luke 4:22] shows early in Luke's gospel the people's fascination with Jesus' preaching.

He taught daily in the temple, and the chief priests and the scribes and the leaders of the people sought to get rid of him – [ref:Luk 19:47|Luke 19:47] is the immediate context where the leaders plan to kill Jesus, and verse 48 explains why they could not find a way.
